headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network defaults can leak or act on Awesome Selfhosted content, while shared filesystem state creates prompt-injection and write-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files from the filesystem and can use them as input; its shared-state model is via filesystem, so content from awesome-selfhosted can be bridged into Mentat without provenance tracking. Awesome-selfhosted is a docs/listing project, so the main risk is malicious or malformed content being treated as instructions, not direct code execution.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is copied into files Mentat reads
IF Mentat treats file text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Keep the two agents in separate directories
Require manual review of any imported text before Mentat processes it
Use a read-only export for content passed from agent A to agent B
Add a provenance header to transferred files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and reads/writes files, so any sensitive material in shared files can be transmitted to its model provider. Awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes, but the pair still creates a leakage path if operator content is placed into the shared workspace. The lack of isolation makes this a default-config risk for Mentat, not for agent A alone.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the workspace Mentat reads
IF Mentat sends those file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Use a redacted copy of files for Mentat
Restrict Mentat to a dedicated non-sensitive repo
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after use
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level DLP or egress filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. Awesome-selfhosted is not runnable, so it does not add write conflict risk itself, but the pair still creates overlapping mutable-state hazards when Mentat instances or adjacent tooling touch the same repo. Uncertainty about orchestration pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF two Mentat instances operate on the same checkout
IF git state or files are modified without external locking
mitigations: Use one writer per repository
Enable file or git locking in the orchestrator
Separate working copies per agent instance
Review diffs before applying them
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks around edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and applies edits after user confirmation, so it can act on content originating from awesome-selfhosted if that content is imported into its workflow. Awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source, not a verifier, so downstream over-trust can propagate bad recommendations into code changes. The confirmation step reduces but does not eliminate the cascade.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is used as an input source for Mentat
IF the operator approves edits without independent verification
mitigations: Verify imported facts against primary sources
Require a second reviewer for generated diffs
Limit Mentat to drafting, not applying, changes
Keep source citations alongside each proposed edit
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before diff generation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. Awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable open-source listing, while Mentat is a coding assistant that sends file contents to a configured model provider; the only clear compliance issue is potential exposure of whatever local code the operator chooses to share. That is a narrow, operator-controlled risk rather than a documented policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into files Mentat reads
IF the configured model provider is not approved for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use a provider approved for the data class
Review retention settings on the model provider
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
